title: write-before-ioctl for key import: correct heap allocation discipline
description: include/uapi/crypto2dev_ioctl.h + src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c — key bytes are not embedded in the ioctl struct. The caller writes raw key bytes to the fd via write(2) into inbuf (heap-allocated to exact key size), then calls KEY_IMPORT which carries only metadata (algo, key_type, keylen, exportable). This is correct for two independent reasons: (1) RSA-4096 PKCS#8 is ~2.4 KB and ML-DSA-87 is 4896 bytes — embedding in an ioctl struct would require a struct large enough for the worst case (currently 8192 bytes), placed on the kernel stack on every KEY_IMPORT call including tiny EC key imports, violating the ~1 KB stack frame guideline; (2) inbuf is allocated exactly to the key size, zeroized and freed after import. A reviewer might suggest embedding keys inline for 'simplicity' — this would cause stack overflow on PQ key imports and violate kernel stack discipline.
